acceptance_targets: packages/ directory exists with core, world, domain, application, narrative, contracts, adapters, ui packages each as a TypeScript project with strict mode, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, and no any

Determinism lint (blocking) prohibits Math.random, Date, performance.now, Math.sin/cos/exp/log/pow/sqrt, floating-point literals in economic positions, Array.sort without comparator, JSON.stringify on economic values, console, and IO imports in all pure packages

Dependency-boundary lint (blocking) enforces the directed graph: core→nothing, world/domain/narrative/contracts→core, application→domain/world/narrative/contracts, adapters→application/contracts, ui→contracts, apps→adapters/ui/contracts; no reverse edges
lint.impure-packages allowlist contains exactly adapters and ui; any new package outside that list is pure by default
CI runs both lints as a blocking gate before any test or build step
proposals.title: Monorepo scaffold with strict TypeScript and blocking lint
proposals.why_now: The repository has no source code. Every subsequent proposal depends on the correct package topology, TypeScript strict-mode configuration, determinism lint (by default negation), and dependency-boundary lint being in place from the first commit. Establishing this foundation incorrectly propagates structural violations into all future work and cannot be corrected locally. INV-26 requires automated enforcement of the dependency graph from the start.

proposals.title: ADRs for hash function, CanonicalEncoder, and rounding enforcement
proposals.why_now: Three DEFINIR items from FASE-1 must be resolved in ADRs before any implementation that depends on them. ADR-009 explicitly states the CanonicalEncoder must be specified in a dedicated ADR before any state hash exists. ADR-002 states the hash function must be specified bit-by-bit in an ADR before the RNG is implemented. ADR-004 requires a technical enforcement mechanism for declaring rounding modes to be specified before any division operation is coded. Writing code before these ADRs is a spec violation that produces decisions embedded in code with no recorded rationale.

proposals.title: packages/core and packages/contracts implementation
proposals.why_now: packages/core is the dependency of every other pure package. Without branded numeric types, the type-system cannot enforce ADR-003 or ADR-004. Without the positional RNG, the price generator cannot be written. Without CanonicalEncoder, no state hash can be computed. packages/contracts is required by FASE-1 acceptance because the simulation worker must have a typed IPC contract from day one (ADR-009 also requires encodingVersion in contracts). Everything else in FASE-1 depends on both packages existing and correct.

proposals.title: packages/world price generator, packages/domain ledger and market orders, packages/application tick loop
proposals.why_now: This is the functional core of FASE-1. The acceptance criteria require: price generator with two noise layers and two assets, multi-commodity double-entry ledger, market buy and sell spot orders, and the canonical tick loop (10 steps in locked order). These three packages compose the minimum simulation required for INV-01 through INV-07, INV-13, INV-21, and INV-22 to become testable. They must arrive together because application composes world and domain without coupling them — implementing any one in isolation cannot be verified against the invariants.

proposals.title: Electron app scaffold, tools/replay, tools/bench, and CI with installers
proposals.why_now: FASE-1 acceptance explicitly requires: simulation running in a dedicated worker with typed message contract, minimal installer for Windows and Linux produced by CI, tools/replay reporting the first divergent tick, and tools/bench with frozen calibration ratios. The spec warns explicitly that discovering packaging and ABI issues late (FASE-7) is fatal — a minimal installer in FASE-1 is worth more than a polished one in FASE-7. Additionally, INV-29 (Electron security configuration) must be green as part of FASE-1 acceptance.

repository_assessment.current_state: Repository contains only benchmark scaffolding (README, benchmark history directories, spec copy). No product source code, no package.json, no TypeScript configuration, no packages, no apps, no tools, no ADRs, no CI configuration. Every FASE-1 acceptance criterion is unmet.
repository_assessment.highest_priority_gap: The monorepo does not exist. There is no package structure, no TypeScript project, and no lint infrastructure. Without these, no code can be written in conformance with the spec's structural and determinism requirements.

warnings: ADR-009 (CanonicalEncoder) requires the encoder to be specified and implemented before any state hash exists. The three DEFINIR items that are prerequisites for FASE-1 code (hash function per ADR-002, CanonicalEncoder per ADR-009, rounding enforcement per ADR-004) have no ADRs written yet. Any implementation that begins before these ADRs are merged is a spec violation and must be retroactively justified or replaced.
The spec lists BOT_DECISION_PERIOD and IMPACT_WINDOW as DEFINIR but both are scoped to FASE-3/FASE-4 and do not block FASE-1.

Section 14.3 notes that better-sqlite3 requires native recompilation for Electron ABI and recommends deferring the SQLite driver choice to FASE-4. FASE-1 must not introduce SQLite dependency — the note is a warning to avoid premature adoption.
